text:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: PAGER fired for tenant=MercuryGames (dedicated pool eu-west-1-reserved-47) — high tail latency + 502 errors. PD# PD-89231. Link: https://observability.redwood.internal/incidents/PD-89231

PagerDuty: page -> oncall@sre (delay 0s)

sre_oncall_Maya: ACK. I'm on it. pulling perf dashboard and logs.

Devon (eng-runtime): saw the alert — 99th latency spike ~3s, error rate 502 up from 0.2% to ~6% over last 5m. KV cache evictions + queue length increasing on reserved-47.

Kenji - SRE Lead: tagging. Is this hitting only MercuryGames?

sre_oncall_Maya: yes, routing table shows tenant header routed to reserved-47. Other tenants on that pool look fine. pattern suggests local capacity throttling/backpressure.

Lina - Support: pinged Mercury CS (Amir) to warn customer and ask about any release they rolled.

Amir - Customer Success: Mercury confirms they pushed a burst of traffic for an in-game event ~10m ago. Might be correlated. They are prepared to throttle if needed.

Devon (eng-runtime): checking instance metrics — GPU utilization at 92% on several nodes, io wait small, but RPS per-slot exceeded reserved throughput. Autoscaler didn't kick because pool at max commit. We have pending queue growth in frontends.

sre_oncall_Maya: quick mitigation options: 1) enable reserved pool burst capacity if permitted; 2) temporary route Mercury to hosted fallback model variant; 3) throttle tenant at gateway (soft-limits) to protect other tenants; 4) evict cold KV cache to free memory (risky).

Kenji - SRE Lead: do option 2 + 3 now. We need to avoid cross-tenant impact. Devon, can you flip routing?

Devon (eng-runtime): preparing route change. will reroute Mercury to hosted-small-quantized-1 model group (latency slightly higher but stable). Applying policy: 
```
route.update --tenant MercuryGames --from reserved-47 --to hosted-fallback:hosted-small-1 --reason "emergency fallback due to reserved pool saturation"
```

Devon (eng-runtime): applied. Confirmed 200 OK from control plane. Starting gradual drain of in-flight requests from reserved-47 for Mercury.

sre_oncall_Maya: enabling soft throttle at edge for Mercury to clamp spike while we validate fallback.

eng-platform: pushed temporary rate-limit rule: 
```
{ "tenant": "MercuryGames", "type": "soft-throttle", "rps": 2500, "window": "60s" }
```

sre_oncall_Maya: monitoring. Dashboard shows Mercury error rate dropping — 502s begin to fall. Latency for other tenants normal.

Lina - Support: Mercury CS confirms fallback is receiving traffic; players reported a short lag but overall OK. They are reducing event intensity.

Devon (eng-runtime): logs from reserved-47 show repeated "kv_cache_eviction: true" entries and a few OOM-kernel fallback messages. Sample log snippet: 
```
[2026-02-26T14:12:01Z] worker-27 ERROR request_handler - allocate_kv_cache failed: OOM
[2026-02-26T14:12:01Z] worker-27 WARN  qdelay=1200ms queue_len=78
[2026-02-26T14:12:02Z] worker-27 ERROR response_sender - downstream 502 gateway_timeout
```

Kenji - SRE Lead: good that fallback worked. Next: we should clear hot cache shards on a couple of nodes to reduce thrashing and coordinate with infra to add one more reserved node if commit allows.

sre_oncall_Maya: will run controlled cache clear on worker-24 and worker-27. Command: 
```
infra-tool exec --cluster reserved-47 --host worker-24 --cmd "redwood-kvcache clear-shard --shard 3" && sleep 10 && check logs
```

Devon (eng-runtime): infra team approved one-off scale: requested burst-add of 1 node in reserved-47. Authorization: Tier D burst allowed per contract — starting add_node job.

Incident Bot: automation: backup routing snapshot created at snapshot://routes/1765436789.

sre_oncall_Maya: cache clear started on worker-24. logs show shard clear completed, qlen dropping.

Kenji - SRE Lead: good. Amir, keep Mercury CS updated and ask them to keep traffic throttle rules until we confirm stability.

Amir - Customer Success: done. Mercury will cap event traffic for next 30m. they appreciate the quick fallback.

Devon (eng-runtime): new node added to reserved-47, joining successfully. GPU pod scheduling done, runtime pods healthy. 

sre_oncall_Maya: monitoring metrics: error-rate -> 0.4%, 99th latency back to baseline for reserved-47 tenants (except Mercury which is on fallback).

eng-platform: reverting soft-throttle config in 10m if stable.

Kenji - SRE Lead: handing the incident to Kenji on-call for follow-up and postmortem. Maya — please add short incident notes and relevant links to PD ticket PD-89231 and create infra follow-up: INFR-3421 (reserved pool burst policy + cache hardening).

sre_oncall_Maya: notes added. PD-89231 acknowledged -> resolved. Created INFR-3421 with action items: 
- investigate KV cache eviction thresholds and aggressive shard clearing side-effects
- add autoscaler override for reserved pools during predictable events
- improve tenant-level telemetry to detect single-tenant bursts earlier

Kenji - SRE Lead: thx team. Final status: customer impacted but mitigated via hosted fallback + soft throttle; reserved pool restored to healthy state. No cross-tenant degradation.

Lina - Support: Mercury will schedule a retro with CS in two days; they requested guidelines on event traffic best practices.

Devon (eng-runtime): will follow up with a small change to route fallback docs and add a safer cache-evict runbook.

Incident Bot: PD-89231 -> RESOLVED by sre_oncall_Maya.

Kenji - SRE Lead: closing thread. follow-ups tracked in INFR-3421. :thumbsup:
